detail.readme:
ArtCraft Launcher

One place to install, update and open every app in the Craft App Suite, rebuilt in pure Rust.
PhotoCraft, LightCraft, FilmCraft, DesignCraft, VectorCraft, PdfCraft, EffectCraft, AniCraft, WordCraft,
DeckCraft, GridCraft, CADCraft, SoundCraft, FigCraft, Craft Anything, TextureCraft, MaterialCraft and the community apps SolidCraft and MailCraft: the right build for your computer, kept up to date.


Download ArtCraft Launcher · ArtCraft · The Craft App Suite

> [!NOTE] > **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Painters, photographers, > filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil > last week. If you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

What it does · Features · Downloads · Build from source · Craft App Suite · Discord


Switch between the grid and a sortable table.

## What it does The Craft apps each ship their own builds for every platform. ArtCraft Launcher saves you from hunting through a dozen release pages: it lists every app in the suite, shows which ones you have and which version, installs the right build for your operating system and processor, and tells you when an update is out. It is a small native app that can sit in your menu bar or system tray. ## Features

📦 Install in one click

Picks the right download for your OS and CPU (DMG, MSI, AppImage, .deb, .rpm and more), checks it against the release's SHA-256 checksums and installs it.

🔄 Stay up to date

Checks each app's GitHub releases and updates the ones you have. A notification tells you when there's something new.

🧭 Always at hand

Opens any Craft app from one window, or from the tray and menu-bar icon. Native egui, no Electron, no web view.
The web version shows the same catalog in the browser, with the latest download for each app. ## Interface languages The interface is in English, Brazilian Portuguese (Português (Brasil)), Czech (Čeština), French (Français), Georgian (ქართული), German (Deutsch), Hungarian (Magyar), Japanese (日本語), Polish (Polski), Russian (Русский), Simplified Chinese (简体中文), Traditional Chinese (繁體中文) or Spanish (Español). **Auto**, the default, follows the system or browser language; **Settings → Language** picks one and switches at once, and the choice is kept between runs. Czech locales (`cs-CZ`, `cs_CZ.UTF-8`…) select Czech, Georgian ones (`ka`, `ka-GE`, `ka_GE.UTF-8`…) Georgian, German ones (`de-DE`, `de-AT`, `de-CH`, `de_DE.UTF-8`…) German, French ones (`fr-FR`, `fr-CA`…) French, Hungarian ones (`hu`, `hu-HU`, `hu_HU.UTF-8`…) Hungarian, Japanese ones (`ja`, `ja-JP`, `ja_JP.UTF-8`…) Japanese, Polish ones (`pl`, `pl-PL`, `pl_PL.UTF-8`) Polish, Spanish ones (`es-ES`, `es-MX`, `es-419`…) Spanish, and Portuguese ones (`pt-BR`, and `pt-PT` too, for now) Brazilian Portuguese. Simplified Chinese locales (`zh-CN`, `zh-SG`, `zh-Hans`, and POSIX forms such as `zh_CN.UTF-8`) select Simplified Chinese; Traditional Chinese ones (`zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, `zh-MO`, `zh-Hant`, and POSIX forms such as `zh_TW.UTF-8`) select Traditional Chinese, with an explicit script winning over the region. To try a language without changing the setting, start the desktop app with `ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_LOCALE=pt-BR`, or add `?lang=ru` to the web address. The CJK languages are drawn with the system's own CJK font (Hiragino Sans or PingFang on macOS, Yu Gothic, Meiryo or Microsoft YaHei on Windows, Noto Sans CJK, IPA, Takao or WenQuanYi on Linux and FreeBSD); Traditional Chinese prefers an installed Noto Sans CJK TC, then PingFang TC, Microsoft JhengHei or MingLiU. Georgian is drawn the same way, with the system's Georgian font (SF Georgian or Arial Unicode on macOS, Sylfaen on Windows, Noto Sans Georgian or DejaVu Sans on Linux and FreeBSD). Where the system has no font for one, and in the web version, the interface stays in English and Settings says why. Product names and release notes stay as published; text without a translation falls back to English. See [`docs/localization-zh-hant.md`](docs/localization-zh-hant.md) for the Traditional Chinese catalog and font details. ## Where apps are installed ArtCraft Launcher installs each app where your system normally keeps applications, using the app's official release package, so an app installed by the launcher is the same as one you installed by hand (and the launcher finds apps you installed yourself): | System | Where | How | |---|---|---| | macOS | `/Applications/.app` | Copied from the signed, notarized release DMG | | Windows | `C:\Program Files\ArtCraft\` (`Program Files (x86)` for a 32-bit build) | The release MSI, through Windows Installer, for everyone on the computer (with Start menu entry and Apps & features entry). Windows asks for administrator permission for each new install. An app already installed for your account only (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ArtCraft\`) keeps its folder and scope when updated; to move it, uninstall it and install it again | | Linux | `/usr/bin`, `/usr/share/applications` | The release `.deb` (apt) or `.rpm` (dnf, zypper), with your system's password prompt. Without those, a Flatpak, or an AppImage in `~/Applications` | | Linux, inside the launcher's Flatpak, with no Flatpak on the host | `~/.var/app/ai.storyteller.artcraft-launcher/data/artcraft-launcher/apps/` | The release tarball, unpacked into the launcher's own folder and run inside the same sandbox, with its settings in a `home/` folder beside it. Nothing is installed on the host, and each app's configuration stays in the sandbox | | FreeBSD | `/usr/local` | The release tree, with a password prompt (polkit); `~/.local` when polkit isn't installed | ArtCraft Launcher keeps itself current too: when a new version is out, **Update and restart** downloads it, verifies it, puts it where this copy is installed (the `.app`, the Windows Installer package or portable folder, the AppImage, or the `.deb`/`.rpm`) and reopens it. Updates use the same format an app was installed with. Every download is checked against the release's published SHA-256 before it is installed, and a running app is never replaced. The launcher writes its log to `logs/artcraft-launcher.log` in its data folder (`~/.local/share/artcraft-launcher` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/ArtCraft Launcher` on macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ArtCraft Launcher` on Windows, `ArtCraftLauncherData` beside the portable zip's executable) and keeps the previous two runs as `artcraft-launcher.1.log` and `artcraft-launcher.2.log`. `RUST_LOG` changes what it records (`debug`, `info,zbus=warn`, …). ## Downloads Download the build for your computer from the [latest release](https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/releases/latest), or browse [all releases](https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/releases). Every release has a `SHA256SUMS.txt` to check the files against. `` is the version number, for example `0.1.0`. **Windows** (10 and 11) | File | What it is | |---|---| | `artcraft-launcher--windows-x64.msi` | Installer for most PCs (Intel and AMD, 64-bit). Installs for the current user, no admin rights needed | | `artcraft-launcher--windows-arm64.msi` | Installer for Windows on Arm (Snapdragon and other Arm PCs) | | `artcraft-launcher--windows-x86.msi` | Installer for 32-bit Windows | | `artcraft-launcher--windows-{x64,arm64,x86}-portable.zip` | No install: unzip and run `artcraft-launcher.exe`. Keeps its settings in the folder | **macOS** (11 Big Sur or later) | File | What it is | |---|---| | `artcraft-launcher--macos-universal.dmg` | Universal app for Apple silicon and Intel Macs, signed and notarized. Drag ArtCraft Launcher to Applications | **Linux** (x86_64 and aarch64; glibc 2.35 or newer, e.g. Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 36+) | File | What it is | |---|---| | `artcraft-launcher--linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.AppImage` | Runs on almost any distro without installing; `chmod +x` and run. The `.AppImage.zsync` beside it lets AppImageUpdate fetch only what changed | | `artcraft-launcher--linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.deb` | Debian, Ubuntu, Mint, Pop!_OS: `sudo apt install ./artcraft-launcher-…deb` | | `artcraft-launcher--linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.rpm` | Fedora, openSUSE, RHEL: `sudo dnf install ./artcraft-launcher-…rpm` | | `artcraft-launcher--linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.flatpak` | Flatpak bundle: `flatpak install --user artcraft-launcher-…flatpak`. Inside the sandbox the launcher installs apps as Flatpaks on the host through `flatpak-spawn --host`; where the host has no Flatpak it falls back to each app's release tarball, unpacked and run inside the sandbox with the app's settings kept in it. Either way it can only reach the host as far as that permission allows; the AppImage, .deb and .rpm builds are the recommended way to run the launcher on Linux | | `artcraft-launcher--linux-{x86_64,aarch64}.tar.gz` | Plain tree (`bin/`, `share/`) for everyone else and for scripts | RISC-V (riscv64): `artcraft-launcher--linux-riscv64.{deb,rpm,tar.gz}`, built against Ubuntu 24.04 (needs glibc 2.39+). The tray icon uses the StatusNotifierItem standard: KDE, Xfce, Cinnamon and most other desktops show it; on GNOME install the AppIndicator extension. **FreeBSD** (14, x86_64) | File | What it is | |---|---| | `artcraft-launcher--freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` | A tree laid out like `/usr/local` | ```sh pkg install libxkbcommon wayland libX11 libXcursor libXrandr libXi libxcb mesa-libs vulkan-loader fontconfig freetype2 tar -xzf artcraft-launcher--freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz --strip-components 1 -C /usr/local artcraft-launcher ``` **Web (WebAssembly)** | File | What it is | |---|---| | `artcraft-launcher-web-.zip` | The catalog as a static site you can host anywhere; see [`packaging/web/README.md`](packaging/web/README.md) | ## Build from source You need a recent stable Rust (1.90 or newer). On Linux, install the windowing headers first (Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo apt install libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev`). ```sh git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher cd craft-launcher cargo run --release -p artcraft-launcher # the desktop app cargo xtask ci # fmt, clippy, tests and the wasm check ``` The web version builds with [trunk](https://trunk-rs.github.io/trunk/): ```sh rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown cd apps/artcraft-launcher-web && trunk serve ``` ### Nix (experimental) `flake.nix` gives a dev shell (`nix develop`, then the cargo commands above) and a package: ```sh nix run github:storytold/craft-launcher ``` On NixOS this uses the system's graphics drivers. On other distros, a Nix-built program can't load the host's GPU drivers, so the window may fail to open. Run it through [nixGL](https://github.com/nix-community/nixGL) instead (NVIDIA needs nixGL's matching NVIDIA variant), or use the AppImage, `.deb` or `.rpm` release: ```sh nix run --impure github:nix-community/nixGL -- nix run github:storytold/craft-launcher ``` ### Installing your own builds To install and update the Craft apps from checkouts on your machine instead of GitHub, clone them next to this repo (`../photocraft`, `../wordcraft`, …) and run: ```sh cargo xtask local sync # git pull every app, build and package each new version into ../local-mirror cargo xtask local serve # serve the builds and a release feed on http://127.0.0.1:8787/ ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_DOWNLOAD_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:8787/ cargo run --release -p artcraft-launcher --features local-mirror ``` Run `sync` again whenever you want updates, or let the server do it: `cargo xtask local serve --sync-every 1h` pulls and builds on that interval while it serves. An app is rebuilt when its checkout's version isn't in the mirror yet (`--rebuild` forces it), and the launcher's next check picks it up. Add `--every-commit` to build every new commit instead, as a dev version between releases (`0.4.0` builds as `0.4.1-dev.`), which the launcher offers as an update. While `ARTCRAFT_LAUNCHER_DOWNLOAD_BASE` is set (loopback addresses only), the launcher asks only the mirror, never GitHub. Only builds with the `local-mirror` feature read it; releases never have it. `cargo xtask local help` lists the options (`--only`, `--no-pull`, `--arch`, …). New contributors and AI agents: start with [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). Release packaging lives in [`packaging/`](packaging/) and [`.github/workflows/release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml). > [!IMPORTANT] > **Status:** ArtCraft Launcher is new and in early alpha. Expect rough edges, and please file > issues (include your OS, which app you were installing and the launcher's log file) or tell us on > [Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft). ## The Craft App Suite Our Discord is where artists of every kind hang out: people who paint, shoot, draw, cut film, set type, and people still figuring out what they like to make.
